title: Data Structures & Algorithms
description: Master problem-solving patterns, computational runtime analysis, memory layouts, trees, graphs, dynamic programming, and interview challenges.

nodes.title: Complexity Analysis (Big O)
nodes.description: Analyze code efficiency in terms of time (operations) and space (RAM). Learn to calculate best, average, and worst-case bounds.
projectIdeas: Write equivalent code blocks for searching an array in O(N) vs O(log N) and plot the execution time difference for large arrays.
interviewQuestions: What is the difference between average case and worst case complexity?

nodes.title: Arrays & LinkedLists
nodes.description: Understand contiguous vs reference memory allocation. Master pointer manipulation, reversing nodes, detection of loops.
projectIdeas: Build a custom singly linked list class in TypeScript that supports inserts, deletes, reversing, and loop detection.
interviewQuestions: Explain why index lookups in an array are O(1) whereas in linked lists they are O(N).
How do you detect a cycle in a linked list?

nodes.title: Stacks & Queues
nodes.description: Learn LIFO/FIFO principles. Implement stacks and queues using arrays and linked lists. Solve dynamic stack sizing and circular queue tasks.
projectIdeas: Implement an undo/redo controller system using a double stack design in TypeScript.
interviewQuestions: Explain how to implement a queue using two stacks.
What is a circular queue buffer?

nodes.title: Searching & Sorting
nodes.description: Master Binary Search, Quick Sort, Merge Sort, and Heap Sort. Learn partitioning strategies and stable vs unstable sorting.

resources.title: Merge Sort vs Quick Sort in 4 mins

projectIdeas: Build an interactive sorting visualizer page demonstrating bubble, merge, and quick sort comparisons.
interviewQuestions: Why is Quick Sort preferred over Merge Sort for arrays?
What is the time complexity of Binary Search and what are its prerequisites?

nodes.title: Recursion & Backtracking
nodes.description: Understand the execution stack, base cases, and state restoration. Solve N-Queens, Sudoku solver, and subset generation.
projectIdeas: Develop an automated maze generator and solver using recursive backtracking on a canvas component.
interviewQuestions: What is a stack overflow and how do base cases prevent it?
Explain the backtracking approach to solving the N-Queens problem.

nodes.title: Trees & Graphs
nodes.description: Master Binary Trees, BST, Traversals (Pre/In/Post order, BFS, DFS), Dijkstra's, MST, and topological sort.
projectIdeas: Build a route finder app using Dijkstra's algorithm on a simulated graph network represented on a 2D canvas.
interviewQuestions: What is the difference between BFS and DFS?
How do you check if a binary tree is a Binary Search Tree?

nodes.title: Heaps & Priority Queues
nodes.description: Master binary heaps, heapify operations, insertion/deletion runtime bounds, and dynamic priority tracking.
projectIdeas: Implement a task scheduling simulation that uses a custom min-heap to queue task execution priorities.
interviewQuestions: Explain the heapify operation and its time complexity.

nodes.title: Greedy Algorithms
nodes.description: Learn global optimization from local choices. Study Huffman Coding, Fractional Knapsack, and Activity Selection problems.
projectIdeas: Build a file compression utility using Huffman Coding mapping ASCII characters to binary pathways.
interviewQuestions: What are the conditions for a problem to be solvable via a greedy approach?
How does the Fractional Knapsack problem differ from the 0/1 version?

nodes.title: Dynamic Programming (DP)
nodes.description: Understand Memoization vs Tabulation. Solve classic knapsack, subsequence, edit distance, and grid traversal problems.
projectIdeas: Solve 10 DP problems on LeetCode and write down a blog/notes explaining the transition states and base cases.
interviewQuestions: What is the difference between Memoization (Top-down) and Tabulation (Bottom-up)?
When can you apply Dynamic Programming to a problem?
